context: Dual-encoded grouped bar chart showing quarterly revenue for 4 product categories, presented side-by-side as Normal Vision and Deuteranopia Simulation panels to demonstrate color+pattern accessibility
first_impression: Clean and purposeful — the side-by-side layout makes the accessibility argument immediately legible without feeling cluttered.
what_works: The dual encoding (color + distinct textures: diagonal hatch, horizontal lines, stipple dots, crosshatch) is genuinely effective — categories remain distinguishable in the deuteranopia panel where colors converge. Four categories stays well within the color overload threshold and the Tol Bright palette provides good perceptual separation.
what_doesnt: The pattern overlay uses low-opacity strokes (rgba 0,0,0,0.22) which are subtle enough that texture differences are harder to read on the shorter bars where bar area is small; stipple dots in particular nearly disappear on low-value bars. The shared legend sits above both panels but describes pattern names in text only — a side-by-side swatch showing the deuteranopia-simulated color alongside the normal color would strengthen the educational message.
